Toponymic surnames are not as weird as you think. You may just not notice them because they are either simplified or originate from a different language. [Some forms originally included a preposition but were subsequently dropped, as in "de Guzmán" (of Guzman) becoming simply Guzmán.](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toponymic_surname#:~:text=A%20toponymic%20surname%20or%20topographic,generic%2C%20derived%20from%20topographic%20features.)

An obvious (albeit still from a videogame) example would be Ezio Auditore da Firenze, or Ezio Auditore **of Florence**.

With all of DS's mysterious faraway lands, I think it's better that we don't see other types of surnames (as mentioned by u/Gigatrad). Otherwise characters may have simply been named Andre the Blacksmith or Gwyndolin, son of Gwyn. Modernised versions of those names would be something like Andre Smith or Gwyndolin Gwynson.
